video_goal: Demonstrate how to accurately test soil pH using the Luster Leaf Rapitest 1605 digital tester.
single_prompt: An overhead view shows hands placing a green Luster Leaf Rapitest 1605 digital tester with a long metal probe and LCD screen, a plastic cup containing dry soil, and a bottle of distilled water onto a flat wooden workbench under bright, even indoor lighting. The camera moves to a close-up as fingers firmly rub an abrasive cleaning pad up and down the metal probe to remove oxidation. From an over-the-shoulder view, a hand pours a steady stream of distilled water into the cup until the soil is fully saturated. In a close-up, a metal spoon vigorously stirs the mixture into a thick, muddy slurry. An extreme close-up shows a thumb pressing the power button on the tester, illuminating the screen with a default number. From an eye-level close-up, a hand pushes the metal probe straight down into the center of the mud slurry. A close-up reveals the hand twisting the tester back and forth to pack the wet soil tightly against the probe. An extreme close-up focuses entirely on the digital screen as numbers rapidly fluctuate up and down, eventually slowing down to lock onto a stable reading of '6.5'. An eye-level close-up shows the hand pulling the tester straight up, extracting the muddy probe from the cup. In a close-up, a white paper towel wipes downward along the probe, removing the mud and leaving the metal shiny. Finally, an extreme close-up shows the thumb pressing the power button one last time, causing the screen to go blank.
